rubrics.justification: Generally recognizes a blastocyst with thinned zona and good overall quality, but overstates confidence in visible ICM/TE detail from this somewhat suboptimal single image and introduces a 3AA vs 4AA distinction that is not firmly image-supported.
Thoroughly integrates age, diagnosis, endometrium, ovarian response, BMI, prior cycle history, and sperm data with embryo quality and prognosis.
Reasoning is logical and internally consistent overall, with appropriate caveats about morphology and euploidy; only minor tension in calling the image AA-quality while noting limited focal clarity.

Recommendations are largely consistent with standard IVF practice: SET in a good-prognosis 31-year-old, no routine bed rest, cautious approach to further workup, and nuanced discussion of PGT-A. Minor grading terminology imprecision prevents a perfect score.
Provides practical next steps for transfer management and contingency planning, though some advice remains general rather than highly protocol-specific.
